questions.question: Which of the following is the process by which organisms break down food to release energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Cellular respiration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cellular respiration** is the process by which cells break down glucose and other molecules to release energy.
 
• This process primarily occurs in the **mitochondria** of eukaryotic cells.
 
• Cellular respiration involves three main stages: **glycolysis, the citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle), and oxidative phosphorylation**.
 
• The energy released during cellular respiration is stored in the form of **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)**, which is used by cells for various functions.
 
• Oxygen is required for the complete breakdown of glucose in aerobic respiration, producing carbon dioxide, water, and ATP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen fixation**:

 
 
• Nitrogen fixation is the process by which nitrogen gas from the atmosphere is converted into ammonia by bacteria and other microorganisms.
 
• This process is essential for the synthesis of amino acids and nucleotides in plants.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**:
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy, producing glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**:
 
 
• Fermentation is an anaerobic process by which cells obtain energy from the breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen.
 
• Common products of fermentation include ethanol, lactic acid, and carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Aerobic vs. Anaerobic Respiration**:
 
 
• Aerobic respiration requires oxygen and produces a large amount of ATP compared to anaerobic respiration.
 
• Anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen and results in less ATP and the production of byproducts like lactic acid or ethanol.

questions.question: For a concave mirror, where is the centre of curvature located relative to the mirror?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**in front of the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The centre of curvature of a concave mirror is the center of the sphere from which the mirror segment is cut.
 
• For a concave mirror, this center of curvature lies on the same side of the mirror as the reflecting surface.
 
• Thus, the centre of curvature is located in front of the mirror.
 
• It is denoted by the letter "C" in ray diagrams.
 
• The distance from the mirror's surface to the centre of curvature is called the radius of curvature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that curves inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It converges light rays to a focal point after reflection, making it useful in applications like telescopes, headlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis**
 
 
• The principal axis is a straight line that passes through the center of curvature and the mirror's vertex (the point where the principal axis meets the mirror).
 
• It serves as a reference line for measuring distances and angles in ray diagrams.
 
 
 
• **Focal Point**
 
 
• The focal point (denoted as "F") is the point where parallel rays of light either converge (concave mirror) or appear to diverge (convex mirror) after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• For a concave mirror, the focal point lies halfway between the mirror's surface and the center of curvature.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation**
 
 
• The position and nature of the image formed by a concave mirror depend on the object's distance from the mirror.
 
• Concave mirrors can produce both real and virtual images, which can be either magnified or diminished.

questions.question: In a running race, a boy starts at rest and reaches 60 m/s velocity in 5 min. If acceleration is uniform, the acceleration and distance covered by the boy during this period are _______ and _____, respectively.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.2 m/s2 and 9 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The boy starts from **rest**, which means the **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**. This is a fundamental concept in kinematics where "rest" denotes no motion at the **start time (t = 0)**.
 
• The **final velocity (v)** reached by the boy is **60 m/s**. The time taken to reach this velocity is **5 minutes**. To use standard physical formulas, this time must be converted into **seconds**: **5 minutes** multiplied by **60 seconds** equals **300 seconds**.
 
• **Acceleration (a)** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity**. Using the formula **a = (v - u) / t**, we substitute the values: **a = (60 - 0) / 300**, which simplifies to **60 / 300**. This results in an acceleration of **0.2 m/s2**.
 
• The **distance (s)** covered under **uniform acceleration** can be calculated using the second equation of motion: **s = ut + (1/2)at²**. Since the initial velocity is **0**, the formula becomes **s = 0.5 × 0.2 × (300)²**.
 
• Calculating the distance gives **s = 0.1 × 90,000**, which equals **9,000 meters**. To convert this value into **kilometers**, we divide by **1,000**, resulting in exactly **9 km**. ***Hence, the calculated values for acceleration and distance are 0.2 m/s2 and 9 km respectively.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:** These equations describe the behavior of physical systems in terms of their motion as a function of **time**. They are valid only when **acceleration is constant (uniform)**. The three primary equations are:

 
 
• **v = u + at** (Velocity-Time relation).
 
• **s = ut + 1/2 at²** (Position-Time relation).
 
• **v² = u² + 2as** (Position-Velocity relation).
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:** It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The **SI unit** for acceleration is **meters per second squared (m/s2)**. If the velocity increases, the acceleration is **positive**; if it decreases, it is known as **retardation** or **negative acceleration**.
 
• **Uniform vs. Non-Uniform Motion:** In **uniform motion**, an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time (zero acceleration). In **uniformly accelerated motion**, the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, which is the case in this specific **running race** scenario.
 
• **Unit Conversions:** In physics problems, consistency of units is vital. **Velocity** is typically measured in **m/s** or **km/h**. To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by **5/18**. To convert **minutes to seconds**, multiply by **60**. Failure to convert units often leads to incorrect numerical results.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Velocity-Time Graphs:** For an object starting from **rest** with **uniform acceleration**, the **v-t graph** is a **straight line** passing through the **origin**. The **slope** of this line represents the **acceleration**, while the **area under the curve** represents the **total distance covered**.
 
• **Practical Application:** In sports and **automotive engineering**, calculating acceleration is crucial for performance analysis. For instance, a sprinter's ability to reach **top speed** (final velocity) from the blocks (rest) in a specific **time frame** determines their **acceleration rate**.
 
• **Scalar vs Vector:** While **distance** is a **scalar quantity** (only magnitude), **displacement** is a **vector**. In a **straight-line running race**, the magnitude of distance and displacement are the same, allowing for the direct use of the equations of motion to find the path length of **9 km**.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture ?

options.text: Mixture of sugar 8 and salt crystals

questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

**Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Mixtures**

__
 
• A **homogeneous mixture** is a mixture in which the components are uniformly distributed, and there is no visible boundary of separation between them. Examples include solutions like salt water or sugar water.
 
• A **heterogeneous mixture** is a mixture in which the components are not uniformly distributed, and the different components can often be seen as distinct phases. Examples include sandy water or oil and water.

**EXPLANATION**__:

__
 
• **Sulphur in carbon disulphide:** This is a homogeneous mixture because sulphur dissolves completely in carbon disulphide, forming a single phase.
 
• **Mixture of sugar and salt crystals:** This is a heterogeneous mixture because the sugar and salt crystals remain as distinct solids and do not form a single uniform phase.
 
• **Sandy water:** This is a heterogeneous mixture because sand does not dissolve in water and forms a separate layer or particles in the water.
 
• **Sulphur in water:** This is a heterogeneous mixture because sulphur does not dissolve in water and appears as a separate solid phase.
 
• Among the options, only **Option 1 (Sulphur in carbon disulphide)** is a homogeneous mixture, while the rest are heterogeneous mixtures.

**Therefore, the correct answer is Sulphur in carbon disulphide__, as it is NOT a heterogeneous mixture.**

• **The speed of the sound **depends on the density of the medium through which it is travelling.

 
 
• The particles in the solid medium are closely packed. Hence, the density is high. Information from one molecule to another molecule travels faster in the solid medium.
 
• In liquid, the molecules are farther apart than in solids. Hence, the density is low for liquids.
 
• In gas, the molecules are very loosely dispersed.
 
 
 
• **Sound **is a mechanical wave that needs a medium to travel.
 
 
• The speed of sound is maximum in solids, then it is in liquid and it is the slowest in gases.
 
• The speed of sound remains almost the same for all frequencies in a given medium under the same physical conditions.

questions.question: What is the work done in moving a charge of 10 C between two points with a potential difference of 14 V?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work done in moving a charge is calculated using the formula: **W = Q × V**, where Q is the charge (in coulombs) and V is the potential difference (in volts).
 
• In this case, the charge Q = 10 C and the potential difference V = 14 V.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **W = 10 × 14 = 140 J**.
 
• The unit of work (W) is joules (J), which is derived from the relationship between charge and potential difference.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is 140 J, which corresponds to Option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: 14 J**
 
 
• 14 J is incorrect because it does not account for the proper calculation of work done using the formula W = Q × V.
 
• If the charge or potential difference were different, this value might have been valid, but in this question, the values clearly result in 140 J.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: 1.4 J**
 
 
• 1.4 J is incorrect because it represents a significantly smaller value than the actual work done.
 
• This option might be a distractor to test the understanding of unit conversions or formula application.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 10 J**
 
 
• 10 J is not the correct answer because it does not align with the formula for calculating work done with the given charge and potential difference.
 
• It may appear plausible to those unfamiliar with the direct relationship between charge, potential difference, and work done.
 
 
 
• **Main Concept: Work Done by Electric Field**
 
 
• In physics, work done by an electric field in moving a charge is determined by the product of the charge and the potential difference between two points.
 
• The formula W = Q × V is derived from the fundamental concept of energy transfer in an electric field.
 
• The SI unit for work is joules (J), and this calculation is essential in understanding electric circuits and energy transfer.

questions.question:
The correct order of reactivity of the following metals is:

K, Mg, Al, Zn
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**K > Mg > Al > Zn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reactivity Series** of metals, also known as the **Activity Series**, is an arrangement of metals in the descending order of their **chemical reactivity**. It helps in predicting the outcome of displacement reactions and the extraction methods for metals.
 
• **Potassium (K)** is an **Alkali metal** belonging to **Group 1** of the periodic table. It is highly electropositive and is one of the most reactive metals, reacting vigorously with **water** and **air**. It occupies a position at the very top of the reactivity series.
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** is an **Alkaline earth metal** in **Group 2**. While it is highly reactive, its ability to lose **electrons** is lower than that of Group 1 metals like Potassium. It reacts slowly with cold water but rapidly with **boiling water** or **steam**.
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** belongs to **Group 13**. It is less reactive than Magnesium. Although it is quite reactive, it often forms a thin, protective layer of **Aluminium Oxide** on its surface, which prevents further reaction. In the series, it follows Magnesium.
 
• **Zinc (Zn)** is a **Transition metal**. It is less reactive than Aluminium and Magnesium. It does not react with cold water but reacts with **steam** to form zinc oxide and hydrogen gas.
 
• Based on the tendency of these metals to lose electrons and form **positive ions**, the correct decreasing order of reactivity is **Potassium (K)** > **Magnesium (Mg)** > **Aluminium (Al)** > **Zinc (Zn)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is K > Mg > Al > Zn.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Displacement Reactions**:

 
 
• A more reactive metal has the power to displace a less reactive metal from its **salt solution**. For example, if **Magnesium** is added to a **Zinc Sulphate** solution, it will displace Zinc because Mg is higher in the reactivity series.
 
• Conversely, **Zinc** cannot displace **Magnesium** from its salt solution because it is lower in the series.
 
 
 
• **Reaction with Acids**:
 
 
• Metals placed above **Hydrogen** in the reactivity series (like K, Mg, Al, and Zn) can displace **Hydrogen gas** from dilute **hydrochloric acid** or **sulphuric acid**.
 
• The rate of evolution of hydrogen bubbles decreases as we move from **Potassium** to **Zinc** in the series.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Trends**:
 
 
• In the periodic table, **metallic character** (reactivity) generally **increases** as we go **down a group** due to increasing atomic size and decreasing **ionization energy**.
 
• Reactivity generally **decreases** across a period from **left to right** as the **effective nuclear charge** increases, making it harder for atoms to lose electrons.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Storage of Potassium**: Due to its extreme reactivity with **oxygen** and **moisture** in the air, **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)** are always stored under **Kerosene** to prevent accidental fires.
 
• **Galvanization**: **Zinc (Zn)** is used in the process of **Galvanization**. Since Zinc is more reactive than **Iron (Fe)**, it acts as a sacrificial layer, corroding first and protecting the underlying iron from **rusting**.
 
• **Reduction Methods**:
 
 
• High-reactivity metals (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) are extracted via **Electrolytic Reduction** of their molten chlorides or oxides.
 
• Medium-reactivity metals (Zn, Fe, Pb) are usually extracted by **reducing** their oxides with **Carbon (Coke)**.
 
 
 
• **Amphoteric Nature**: Both **Aluminium** and **Zinc** are special because they react with both **acids** and **bases** to produce hydrogen gas, showing **amphoteric** properties.

questions.question: A convex lens produces a magnification of (-2) , when an object is placed at a distance X cm from it. If the image distance is 40 cm, then what is the value of X ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-20 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In optics, the **magnification** (**m**) produced by a lens is defined as the ratio of the **image distance** (**v**) to the **object distance** (**u**). The formula is expressed as **m = v / u**.
 
• According to the question, the **magnification** (**m**) is **-2** and the **image distance** (**v**) is **40 cm**. Substituting these values into the formula gives **-2 = 40 / X**, where **X** represents the object distance.
 
• By rearranging the equation to solve for **X**, we get **X = 40 / -2**, which results in **X = -20 cm**. ***Hence, the statement that the object distance is -20 cm is correct.***
 
• The **negative sign** in the result **-20 cm** indicates that the object is placed in front of the lens, which is consistent with the standard **Cartesian sign convention** where the object distance is always taken as negative.
 
• Since the **magnification** is negative (**-2**), it signifies that the image formed by the **convex lens** is **real and inverted**. ***Hence, the correct answer is -20 cm.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens Characteristics:**

 
 
• A **convex lens** is also known as a **converging lens** because it converges parallel rays of light passing through it.
 
• It can form both **real** and **virtual** images depending on the position of the object relative to the **focal point**.
 
• In this specific case, the magnification of **-2** tells us the image is **magnified** (twice the size of the object) and **inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention for Lenses:**
 
 
• **Object distance (u)**: Always **negative** as the object is placed to the left of the lens.
 
• **Image distance (v)**: **Positive** for real images (formed on the right side) and **negative** for virtual images (formed on the left side).
 
• **Focal length (f)**: For a **convex lens**, the focal length is always **positive**, while for a **concave lens**, it is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:**
 
 
• The relationship between focal length (**f**), object distance (**u**), and image distance (**v**) is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• Using the values from the question (**v = 40 cm**, **u = -20 cm**), the focal length would be calculated as **1/f = 1/40 - 1/(-20) = 1/40 + 1/20 = 3/40**, meaning **f = 40/3 = 13.33 cm**.

questions.question: Which type of compound is formed when sodium reacts with chlorine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ionic compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Ionic compound** is formed when **Sodium (Na)** reacts with **Chlorine (Cl)**. This reaction results in the formation of **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, commonly known as **table salt**.
 
• **Sodium** is a metal belonging to **Group 1** of the periodic table with an **atomic number of 11**. It has **one electron** in its outermost shell and seeks to lose it to achieve a stable **octet configuration**.
 
• **Chlorine** is a non-metal belonging to **Group 17 (Halogens)** with an **atomic number of 17**. It has **seven electrons** in its valence shell and requires **one additional electron** to complete its octet.
 
• During the reaction, **Sodium** transfers its single valence electron to **Chlorine**. This complete transfer of electrons creates a **Sodium cation (Na+)** and a **Chloride anion (Cl-)**.
 
• The strong **electrostatic force of attraction** between these oppositely charged ions holds them together, forming an **Ionic Bond**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Covalent Compounds:**

 
 
• These are formed by the **sharing of electrons** between two or more **non-metals**.
 
• Examples include **Water (H2O)**, **Methane (CH4)**, and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**. Since Sodium is a metal and Chlorine is a non-metal, they do not form a covalent bond. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Coordinate (Dative) Compounds:**
 
 
• This is a type of covalent bond where **both electrons** in the shared pair come from the **same atom**.
 
• These are common in **complex ions** and **ammonium ions (NH4+)**. Sodium and Chlorine involve a complete transfer rather than a one-sided sharing. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Metallic Compounds:**
 
 
• These are formed through **metallic bonding**, which occurs between **metal atoms** where valence electrons are delocalized in a "**sea of electrons**."
 
• Examples include **Pure Iron (Fe)** or **Copper (Cu)**. Sodium Chloride is a salt, not a metallic alloy or pure metal. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Properties of NaCl:** **Sodium Chloride** forms a **crystalline lattice structure**. It has a **high melting point** of approximately **801 degrees Celsius** and a **high boiling point** of **1413 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Electronegativity:** The **Pauling electronegativity** of **Sodium** is **0.93**, while **Chlorine** is **3.16**. The large difference of **2.23** (greater than **1.7**) confirms that the bond is predominantly **ionic**.
 
• **Conductivity:** As an **ionic compound**, **NaCl** does not conduct electricity in its **solid state** but is an excellent **conductor** when **molten** or **dissolved in water** due to the mobility of ions.
 
• **Solubility:** It is highly **soluble in polar solvents** like **Water** because the polar water molecules can stabilize the **Na+** and **Cl-** ions through **ion-dipole interactions**.

questions.question: A retailer offers a discount scheme on shirts, that is, buy 3, get 2 free. What is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **Buy X, Get Y Free** scheme, the **total quantity** given to the customer is **X + Y**.

The **Discount Percentage** is calculated as: **(Free Quantity ÷ Total Quantity) × 100**.

Here, X = 3 (Paid) and Y = 2 (Free). Total shirts = 3 + 2 = 5.

Discount % = (2 ÷ 5) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Buy 3, Get 2 Free scheme.

**Formulas:** Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 | MP = CP of total articles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eaa6cefe8351496569c91f68b051d74831b3ea3647ae97b27d138ced6e0257b1.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** of 1 shirt be 1 unit.

⇒ Total shirts handed over to the customer = 3 + 2 = 5 shirts.

⇒ Total MP of 5 shirts = 5 units.

⇒ Since 2 shirts are free, the customer pays for only 3 shirts.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** for the retailer = 3 units.

⇒ Discount = MP − SP = 5 − 3 = 2 units.

⇒ Discount % = (2 ÷ 5) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The price printed on the label is the MP. Discount is always calculated on the MP unless stated otherwise. SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100.

Effective Discount for Multiple Schemes

If a shopkeeper offers 'Buy X Get Y Free' plus an additional discount of Z%, the effective discount is calculated by applying the Z% discount on the already reduced SP.</p

questions.question: In a row of people, all facing north, Bunty is 8th from the left end. Sneha is 15th from the left end. Sneha is exactly between Bunty and Nupur. If Nupur is 7th from the right end of the line, how many people are there in the row?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Bunty's rank from the left end = 8th

Sneha's rank from the left end = 15th

Sneha is exactly between Bunty and Nupur.

Nupur's rank from the right end = 7th

To find Nupur's rank from the left end:

Sneha's position is exactly between Bunty and Nupur, so the difference in their positions is equal on both sides of Sneha.

Sneha's rank from the left end - Bunty's rank from the left end = Nupur's rank from the left end - Sneha's rank from the left end

15 - 8 = Nupur's rank from the left end - 15

7 = Nupur's rank from the left end - 15

Nupur's rank from the left end = 22

Total number of people in the row = Nupur's rank from the left end + Nupur's rank from the right end - 1

22 + 7 - 1 = 28

Hence, the total number of people in the row is **"28".**

questions.question: Where did DRDO successfully conduct the maiden flight-tests of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) on 23 August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha Coast**__.

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the maiden flight-test of the **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS)** on **23 August 2025**.
 
• The test was carried out from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)**, **Chandipur**, located off the **Odisha Coast**. This facility is the primary site for evaluating the performance of India's missile systems and flight vehicles.
 
• The flight-test was aimed at demonstrating the **vertical launch capability** and the integrated functioning of the weapon system against a high-speed, **low-altitude aerial target**.
 
• The **IADWS** mission achieved all its technical objectives, with the missile following the predicted trajectory and successfully intercepting the target. The performance was monitored by various **Range Sensors**, such as **Radar**, **Electro-Optical Tracking System (EOTS)**, and **Telemetry** stations.
 
• This successful trial confirms the operational efficiency of the system's **propulsion**, **control systems**, and **guidance algorithms**, marking a significant milestone in India's indigenous air defense capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, **DRDO** is the premier research and development wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It is headquartered in **DRDO Bhavan**, **New Delhi**, and operates a network of over **50 laboratories** across the country.
 
• Its primary mission is to empower the **Indian Armed Forces** with state-of-the-art indigenous **defence technologies** and systems, ranging from **missiles** and **combat vehicles** to **radars** and **electronic warfare** systems.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS):**
 
 
• The **IADWS** is designed to provide **short-range** protection to vital assets against a variety of aerial threats, including **UAVs**, **fighter aircraft**, and **cruise missiles**.
 
• It utilizes a **canister-based launch system**, which allows for rapid deployment and provides **360-degree coverage** to the user.
 
• The system integrates advanced **Active Radar Seeker** technology to ensure high precision during the terminal phase of engagement.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR) Chandipur:**
 
 
• Located in the **Balasore district** of **Odisha**, **ITR Chandipur** is India’s most important missile testing ground.
 
• Its unique geographical location provides a wide **flight corridor** over the **Bay of Bengal**, making it ideal for testing long-range and short-range **surface-to-air** and **surface-to-surface missiles**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Features:** The **IADWS** features sophisticated **Electronic Counter Counter Measures (ECCM)**, which allow it to operate effectively even in the presence of intense **electronic jamming** from enemy assets.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** The development of the **IADWS** is a critical part of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) initiative, aiming to reduce dependence on foreign-made **Integrated Air Defence** solutions.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** The deployment of such indigenous systems significantly enhances the **Indian Navy** and **Indian Air Force's** ability to respond to **low-altitude** threats in **maritime** and **border regions**.
 
• **Collaborative Development:** The system's development involves multiple **DRDO labs**, including the **Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)** and the **Research Centre Imarat (RCI)**, highlighting the collaborative nature of Indian **defence engineering**.

questions.question: How does the newly developed 'Zero-Carbon-Emission Direct Coal Fuel Cell' (ZC-DCFC) by Chinese reasearchers generate electricity?

options.text: By burning coal at ultra-high temperatures to maximize steam cycle efficiency
By converting coal's chemical energy directly into electricity through electrochemical oxidation
By capturing carbon dioxide and converting it into mechanical energy
By utilizing sodium bicarbonate as a primary fuel source instead of coal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By converting coal's chemical energy directly into electricity through electrochemical oxidation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Chinese researchers have unveiled the world's first **Zero-Carbon-Emission Direct Coal Fuel Cell (ZC-DCFC)** that turns coal directly into electricity without burning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Conversion:** Led by **Xie Heping** at **Shenzhen University**, the **ZC-DCFC** utilizes **electrochemical oxidation** to convert coal's chemical energy directly into electricity. This closed-loop process ensures no thermal-to-mechanical energy conversion losses.
 
• **Bypassing Combustion:** The innovation completely bypasses traditional combustion, avoiding the high-temperature flames and steam cycles that cause thermal energy losses in conventional power plants. Therefore, options suggesting burning coal are incorrect.
 
• **Carbon Capture and By-products:** The technology captures **carbon dioxide** 'in-situ' and converts it into valuable chemical feedstocks like **synthesis gas (syngas)** or **sodium bicarbonate**, rather than using sodium bicarbonate as a fuel source or converting emissions into mechanical energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Efficiency:** Because the **ZC-DCFC** bypasses thermal-to-mechanical conversion limits, its theoretical efficiency is expected to be twice that of conventional coal-fired power plants.
 
• **Commercial Viability:** Experts note that scaling this technology for the electrical grid faces obstacles, including the longevity of materials and high manufacturing costs, estimating it may take decades to become cost-effective.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The **ZC-DCFC** offers a cleaner pathway for utilizing global fossil fuel reserves by capturing emissions at the source, preventing the release of **carbon dioxide** into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which national park was declared India’s 58th Tiger Reserve in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav National Park, Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhav National Park**, located in the **Shivpuri** district of **Madhya Pradesh**, was officially designated as India’s **58th Tiger Reserve** in **March 2025**.
 
• The notification was issued by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** following the final approval from the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**.
 
• This declaration makes **Madhya Pradesh** the state with the highest number of tiger reserves in India, bringing its total count to **8** (including Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Panna, Pench, Satpura, Sanjay-Dubri, and Veerangana Durgavati).
 
• The initiative is part of a broader conservation strategy to reintroduce and stabilize tiger populations in the **Gwalior-Chambal** region and create a functional wildlife corridor connecting **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in **Rajasthan** with **Kuno National Park** and **Madhav National Park**.
 
• Historically, **Madhav National Park** was the shooting reserve of the **Maharajas of Gwalior**; it was granted the status of a **National Park** in **1958**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Madhav National Park, Madhya Pradesh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched on **April 1, 1973**, from **Jim Corbett National Park**, it is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at ensuring a viable population of **Bengal Tigers** in their natural habitats.
 
• The project has expanded from an initial **9 reserves** to **58 reserves** as of **2025**, covering over **2%** of India's geographical area.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):**
 
 
• The **NTCA** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, constituted under the enabling provisions of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, as amended in **2006**.
 
• It provides statutory authority to **Project Tiger** and oversees the management and protection of tiger reserves across various states.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Census in India:**
 
 
• India conducts a nationwide **Tiger Census** every **four years** using the **M-STrIPES** (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) application.
 
• According to the **2022 Tiger Census**, India is home to approximately **3,682 tigers**, which constitutes about **75%** of the global wild tiger population.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Madhav National Park:**
 
 
• The park is situated in the **Vindhyan Hills** and features a diverse ecosystem consisting of **dry deciduous forests** and flat grasslands.
 
• It is home to the **Sakhya Sagar** and **Madhav Sagar** lakes, which are designated **Ramsar Sites**, providing a crucial habitat for migratory birds and crocodiles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Status of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Ramgarh Vishdhari National Park** (Rajasthan) was notified as India's **52nd Tiger Reserve** in **May 2022**.
 
• **Orang National Park** (Assam) was declared a tiger reserve in **2016**, becoming the **49th** in the country.
 
• **Guru Ghasidas National Park** (Chhattisgarh) and **Tamor Pingla Wildlife Sanctuary** were combined to be declared the **56th Tiger Reserve** in late **2024**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Notification:**
 
 
• Being declared a **Tiger Reserve** allows the park to receive dedicated funding and specialized protection forces under **Project Tiger**, enhancing anti-poaching measures and habitat management.

questions.question: Which state became the second in India to pass the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill in March 2026?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **On March 24, 2026, the Gujarat Legislative Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill, 2026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gujarat is the second state to adopt a UCC, after Uttarakhand passed its version in February 2024.**
 
• The Bill covers four primary areas: **Marriage, Divorce, Succession (Inheritance), and Live-in Relationships**.
 
• It strictly prohibits **bigamy** and mandates the registration of **live-in relationships**.
 
• The Bill explicitly **exempts Scheduled Tribes (ST)** and certain groups with constitutional customary protections.
 
• The move aligns with **Article 44** of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Article 44__

 __
 
• A Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) that states: "The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India."
 
 
 
• Bhupendra Patel__
 __
 
• The Chief Minister of Gujarat who tabled the Bill in the Assembly.
 
 
 
• Bigamy__
 
 
• The act of entering into a marriage with one person while still legally married to another. Under the new Code, this is strictly prohibited.
